$comment: The block request wire (F-027-dc, ADR-0093 amendment 2026-09-27) — the
declared home of the routing key the lease planner asks billing for a
metered block under, of every field in that message, and of the figures
the wallet reserve is computed to on both sides.
network-service writes it in Go and billing-service reads it in
TypeScript; neither can import the other, so this fixture plus a test on
each side replaces the import that does not exist (ADR-0036, C-08). The Go
Its own prefix, not network.usage.: metering-service binds network.usage.#
and dead-letters any key there that is not a pass or a release.
purchasedBytes is the bag the planner saw. Billing buys only while the
Grant still holds exactly that figure: a request that arrives after another
block was bought is stale, and is dropped rather than bought twice.
affordable is bytesAffordable(rate, cachedBalance), rate the vpn.traffic meter's unitPrice: whole cents of
the balance, floored, over the rate per 2^30 bytes, floored. Go computes the
reserve it adds to Quota with it (ADR-0094 amendment); billing prices the
block with it. Both sides are checked against these rows.
